title: Your body makes 2 million blood cells every second 🩸 #shorts
description:
Your bone marrow makes over 2 million new red blood cells every second. Each lives about 120 days, and at any moment around 25 trillion are circulating — more than all your other cells combined.
Sources: Stanford Blood Center (2 million/second, ~120 days); Sender, Fuchs & Milo 2016, PLOS Biology (~25 trillion red blood cells, ~84% of human cells).

Inner Numbers — your body, counted. New Short every day.
Educational content, not medical advice.

scenes.say: In the last second, your body made two million new red blood cells.
They're built deep inside your bones.
Each one lives for about one hundred and twenty days.
Right now, around twenty five trillion of them are moving through you.
That's more than all your other cells put together.
And it never stops. Follow for more of your body, counted.
